required_changes_injected: CRITERION 2 VIOLATION — Carry-forward consistency broken. Decision Criteria and Identified Pain both regressed from 8/10 and 7/10 (cumulative state) to 5/10 in this analysis, with justification that 'locked score per final scoring instruction' overrides carry-forward rules. This is invalid. The rubric states carry-forward rules apply unless recent call contradicts prior assessment. The July 9 call does NOT contradict the eight technical criteria (warehouse-native, BigQuery, SSO, Drupal, SDKs, all-in-one, self-hosting, privacy) or the four pain points (personalized journeys, BigQuery costs, marketer/developer balance, segmented targeting). The July 9 call simply does not mention them — which is not contradiction. Per Criterion 2, unchanged components must maintain prior scores with explicit note 'No new information — maintaining previous assessment.' Decision Criteria should remain 8/10 with note that June criteria stand uncontradicted. Identified Pain should remain 7/10 with same reasoning. CRITERION 4 VIOLATION — Next steps for Decision Criteria and Identified Pain use vague language: 'ask' without specific contact action verb. Example: 'ask the prospect directly: When your team sits down...' lacks concrete action (e.g., 'Schedule call with [contact TBD] by Sept 5 to ask'). Rewrite as: '[contact TBD]: Schedule evaluation framework discussion by Sept 5 — ask: When your team evaluates GrowthBook versus alternatives, what are the two or three must-haves?' CRITERION 1 — All components present with status and score; evidence provided for all. CRITERION 3 — Evidence quality acceptable; Optimizely confirmed in competitive set; no seller-stated ROI claimed. CRITERION 5 — No unsupported claims; ICP fit not explicitly confirmed but not disqualified (BigQuery, personalization, experimentation signals present; no explicit disqualifiers). Fix: Restore Decision Criteria to 8/10 and Identified Pain to 7/10 with carry-forward notes, and rewrite next steps with concrete action verbs and contact/deadline specificity.
